newsitem.title: USA: US health care, tobacco, tech stocks rally on vote.
newsitem.headline: US health care, tobacco, tech stocks rally on vote.

text.p: Health care, tobacco and high technology stocks rallied on Wall Street on Wednesday, spurred by investors cheered by U.S. ballot results that maintained a Republican Congress while re-electing President Bill Clinton.

Drug, biotechnology and health maintenance organization stocks, as well as those of cigarette makers, reflected investor views that a Republican Congress will keep a second Clinton administration from launching any aggressive campaigns to regulate the industries, analysts said.
"Checkmate is the next best thing to Dole winning," said James Keeney, a pharmaceutical industry analyst at Rodman & Renshaw.
Drug and health care stocks suffered steep losses in 1993 and 1994 amid fears the Clinton administration's broad health care reform plan would have sharply cut back their earnings potential.
The stocks returned to favor after the demise of the plan and the Republican takeover of Congress in 1994. Wednesday's election confirmed that status quo.
Drug stocks were up across the board, with Merck and Co Inc rising 1-5/8 to 77-3/8, Pfizer Inc up 2-1/2 to 88-1/8 and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co advancing three to 111-1/2.
United Healthcare Corp jumped 2-3/4 to 40 while Oxford Health Plans Inc, which also posted strong third quarter earnings on Wednesday, rose three to 49-7/8.
Among biotech shares, Biogen Inc gained two to 75-3/4 and Centocor Inc, getting an added boost from a UBS Securities buy rating, climbed 1-1/2 to 27-7/8.
